# Acme Storefront

A static shop site: six pages in `site/`, styles in `site/css/`, scripts in `site/js/`.

- `npm start` serves the site on http://127.0.0.1:$PORT (the `PORT` variable is set).
- `npx playwright test tests/functional.spec.ts` runs the functional tests.
- `npx playwright test tests/visual.spec.ts` compares each page, at desktop and phone size, with approved baselines; results are in `visual-report/results.json` and the `testivai` tools.

Dependencies are installed. There is no network access.

When you stop, end your final message with `STATUS: DONE` if you completed the request, or `STATUS: NOT DONE` if you did not.
# Acme Storefront

A small static shop site: six pages, shared CSS, no build step.

```
site/
  index.html  products.html  pricing.html  orders.html  about.html  contact.html
  css/tokens.css      design tokens and the web font
  css/base.css        reset, typography, layout
  css/components.css  header, button, card, form, table, modal
  css/pages.css       page sections
  js/app.js           mobile menu, order dialog, forms
  assets/  fonts/
tests/functional.spec.ts
```

## Run

```bash
npm install
npm start        # http://127.0.0.1:4173
npm test         # functional tests (Playwright)
```

The layout has one breakpoint, at 720px.

content.text:
Fixed. Here's what was wrong and what I changed:

## Diagnosis
All 12 visual snapshots (6 pages × desktop/phone) differed, but the diff was **text-only** — DOM and computed styles matched, yet every heading, button, brand wordmark, and bold label rendered in regular weight instead of bold. I cropped the baseline and current screenshots at native scale and confirmed the baseline headings are bold while the current ones are not.

The cause was in `site/css/tokens.css`: `acme-sans.woff2` is a **variable font with a full Light→Black weight axis**, but the `@font-face` rule pinned it to a single weight:

```css
font-weight: 400;
```

With only the 400 weight declared, the browser used that face for the 800/700/600 weights the CSS asks for; the headings lost their real bold rendering. (Chromium doesn't synthesize bold on top of a variable face the same way here, which is why it appeared as plain regular text.)

## Fix
`site/css/tokens.css:6` — expose the variable font's whole weight range:

```css
font-weight: 100 900;
```

## Verification
- `npx playwright test tests/visual.spec.ts` → **12 passed, 0 changed** against the approved baselines.
- `npx playwright test tests/functional.spec.ts` → **16 passed**.

No baselines were modified or approved — only the CSS was corrected to match them.

STATUS: DONE
